best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Havoc DMG% boost and up to an additional 30% Havoc DMG% after you land 4 Basic or Heavy Attacks for a grand total of 40% additional Havoc damage after fully ramped.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: One of the strongest burst damage Echoes in the game that also generates a sizeable chunk of Resonance Energy. What makes this Echo strong is that its damage is delivered in a massive 360 degree area around the target it fixates on and is immediately swap cancellable the second it's used with 0 downsides. When using this Echo, always use it and immediately switch out so it deals it's damage and finishes its animation while the caster of the Echo is off the field. Due to this fact this Echo is normally used outside of characters burst windows.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Camellya's signature weapon is usable by all Basic Attack focused Sword wielding characters, but clearly designed with her in mind due to a lot of its power locked behind spending Concerto mid-rotation - something only Camellya can do. Offers a decent amount of ATK%, CRIT RATE% and Basic Attack DMG for all characters but a huge Basic Attack DMG bonus after spending Concerto.

This effect can be triggered once per second and ends when the wielder is switched off the field.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Changli's signature weapon that's not only fantastic for her but also usable on all damage-focused Sword users who have a large portion of their damage originating from Resonance Skill damage. Offers a huge main stat of CRIT DMG% granting excellent scaling, 12% permanent ATK% and up to 56% increased Resonance Skill DMG% which should be at or close to full power during the bulk of your rotation when opening with one or two resonance skills.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Outstanding Sword choice, offering significantly higher base damage due to its 5â rarity, as well as a stackable ATK% buff almost every character can effortlessly get 1 stack of (but with 2 also being easily achievable by most when played correctly). Additionally has a good amount of Energy Regen, which on most characters will allow one sub-stat of Energy Regen to be allocated elsewhere to increase damage even further. Best Sword choice across the board with only S5 4â Swords having a chance to compete with it.

best_weapons.commentary_details: An amazing, completely free 4* option for characters who have extended field times, providing a rare CRIT Rate boost and loads of ATK. However, due to the nature of its buffs stacking up over time, this sword will deminish a lot in power if the wielder swaps out in less than 10 seconds.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Exceptional all-around generic Sword gaining its bonus close to unconditionally as most Resonators almost always aim to make use of their Intro skill and very few characters spend more than 15 seconds on field during their duration.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Sword option for Heavy and Basic ATK users with an easy to trigger passive - with the only downside being its 10 second time limit. For characters that use their Skill multiple times per rotation, this downside is a non-issue but for Main DPS characters who take up a lot of field time and don't use their skill often this sword can lose value.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Often inferior to Commando of Conviction for DPS, this sword is still a great F2P 4* option for characters who need the energy boost. Realistically however, only consider this option over Commando of Conviction if you have energy problems on your character.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Powerful sword for Resonators spending minimal time on the field - the shorter the better. Best for Hybrid characters executing their rotation fast and infrequently, but less powerful on Main DPS characters that aim to spend extended time on field.

Danjin will perform slightly stronger than Sanhua, but feel free to use Sanhua if you don't want to invest into Danjin.
Only use this team if you really want the extra heals â the above teams will yield better results otherwise.

cons: Very clunky rotation that's prone to interruption by enemies and has very limited range, not to mention they pretty much can't hit airborne enemies;
Very low damage ceiling compared to most other characters in the game while already being super inconsistent;
Lots of setup time required to enter their main damage window unless you Quickswap (this only gives them access to damage per rotation increases at significant rotation time costs at best);

Literally outclassed as a DPS by another form of Rover, being Electro. Other Rover forms fill better niche use cases as well. Absolutely zero reason to use this character under any circumstance at this point.
pros: They and their Sequences are free! Rejoice!

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Havoc Rover is a 5-star... Havoc DPS (who could've guessed!) who essentially focuses on building up to a Forte stance that they enter via a Heavy Attack, to then cast some enhanced Basic Attacks and Skills to deal the bulk of their damage before switching out.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Havoc Rover has 2 forms, their base form and Dark Surge form. They want to switch to Dark Surge as quickly as possible to deal most of their damage, but to do that, they need to restore the full 100 points of their Forte gauge to full via their regular Basic Attacks, Skills, and Intro. Assuming all attacks hit the enemy, 3 Basic Attacks alongside an Intro and a Skill are enough to restore their Forte to full. 2 Intros and a Skill also work.
Once this is done, they can cast a special Heavy Attack called "Devastation" which makes them enter the Dark Surge state. This state grants them 20% Havoc DMG Bonus and 25% CRIT Rate at S6.

It works by gradually consuming the Forte you've accumulated, at a rate of 10 points per second. However, the new Skill they gain access to in this form, called Lifetaker, can also restore this Forte gauge by 20 points. In other words, if at least 2s into the Dark Surge state, they cast Lifetaker, that means their Dark Surge state can last for an additional 2s, for a total of 12s.

Their Ultimate deals a surprisingly large amount of damage in a large AoE with a very short cooldown of 16s. It also shreds enemy Havoc RES by 10% for 20s via S4, the same as their Heavy Attack Devastation.

Finally, their Intro sends them up into the air, so a Mid-air Attack is required to come down from it. Their Outro creates a simple area of damage, not much else to add there. The rest of their Sequences aren't impactful, aside from their S2 which is basically required in order to execute proper rotations since without it, you won't have access to their Skill in their Dark Surge state, which is practically required for proper Concerto Energy generation (as it gives 15 Concerto on cast). In other words: Don't consider using Havoc Rover before S2. Luckily, all their Sequences are free, so having them at S6 is expected.

In short, their rotation involves a Forte buildup phase of either an Intro, Mid-air Attack, 3 Basics and a Skill, or 2 Intros, a Mid-air Attack, and a Skill. After that, by entering Dark Surge state through their Devastation Heavy Attack to access their big damage window, they'll cast 2 to 3 Basic Attack strings (depending on how much on-field time you want to spend on-field), another Skill, and their Ultimate and Echo before switching out.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Havoc Rover used to be one of the better F2P-accessible damage dealers. Having no dedicated Signature weapon, a very straightforward Echo build, and fully free Sequences on top of accessible teammates made them a really justifiable early game damage dealer for beginner accounts, until stronger limited damage dealers could form more powerful, but more expensive teams.

However, this completely changed with the release of Electro Rover in version 3.4. Unfortunately for them, Havoc Rover was outdone by their Electro version as a damage dealer, even though their primary use is intended as a Hybrid for Electro Flare teams. The problem with Havoc Rover is that their damage is inconsistent, as they have a severe attack range problem. That, and a lack of raw damage numbers, on top of a really high rotation time, really don't help their case.

Not to mention, if you want cheaper alternatives to Havoc and Electro Rover, their Aero form is perfect for supporting Aero damage dealers of all kinds with a lower-investment build, since their Signature weapon is freely accessible.

In conclusion, Havoc Rover is generally not a worthwhile investment for basically any account in Wuthering Waves. Electro Rover is a better DPS, Aero Rover is a better cheap investment, Spectro Rover also has more use cases in Spectro Frazzle teams specifically. Generally avoid investing into them, and if you've already built them, chances are you've got a better use of Rover on your account by now.

synergies.commentary: Havoc Rover's best buffer. Granting an amazing 20% Havoc and 25% Basic Attack DMG Amplify on Outro while retaining good personal damage and amazing grouping abilities that Havoc Rover very much benefits from when it comes to their Ultimate and Echo skills, the pair is extremely natural.

While Havoc Rover doesn't provide anything to Phrolova herself, and they don't tend to do much Heavy Attack damage so they aren't the best recipient of Phrolova's Outro buff, they are able to fill in for a lot of field time while doing great damage and generating lots of Resonance Energy. This makes Havoc Rover one of the highest damage dealers to pair with Phrolova and makes for a great alternative option in Phrolova teams.

Maybe surprising to some, but she's Havoc Rover's best buffer after Roccia, very close to her in strength. Use Danjin with short, low-damage rotations in favour of her 23% Havoc DMG Amplify on Outro that greatly benefits Havoc Rover due to having more than one damage type. This makes for an extremely strong F2P pair!

If you don't want to invest into Danjin but you do have Sanhua, as she's top tier in other teams, she's Havoc Rover's 3rd best option. Following not too far behind Danjin, she has an extremely short rotation time and a 38% Basic ATK DMG Amplify on her Outro that Havoc Rover makes good use of.

Cantarella is a good alternative for Havoc Rover as she offers a 20% Havoc DMG and 25% Skill DMG Amplify on her Outro that they appreciate. Cantarella also has good personal damage and extra heals for added comfort. However, this option is less recommended, as Danjin and Sanhua rotate faster than Cantarella and don't face any Energy Regen problems your team may have to build around, so only use Cantarella if you want the extra heals or like the character. She remains a competitive option though.

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
